research_question: How does the non-removable lateral registry inversion asymmetry of the published 2H Janus MoSSe GSFE translate into prepared-state directional depinning and zero-mean vector transport in an unguided finite two-dimensional contact, and which parts of that response survive geometry changes, thermal noise, and in-plane compliance?
central_thesis: Within a DFT-anchored reduced finite-contact model, non-removable registry inversion asymmetry produces prepared-state direction-split unguided depinning; same-spectrum symmetry controls identify that asymmetry as the source of the directional response, while compact-contact scaling, boundary-state competition, vector locking, thermal statistics, and in-plane relaxation define the regimes in which the effect persists and the boundaries beyond which it has not been established.

paper_argument_map.problem: Twist suppresses corrugation in finite van der Waals contacts, but residual finite-contact pinning can remain direction dependent when the lateral registry landscape is not inversion symmetric.
paper_argument_map.gap: The published Janus MoSSe lateral GSFE had not been connected through a coordinate-independent symmetry test to unguided prepared-state full-2D rectification, matched mechanism falsification, geometry dependence, vector locking, thermal hierarchy, and in-plane compliance within one evidence chain.
paper_argument_map.approach: Published three-shell GSFE -> unguided lowest-energy prepared contact -> branch depinning -> matched symmetrization/exact inversion -> compact geometry and in-plane relaxation -> boundary registry competition -> deterministic rocking -> stationary thermal inference.
paper_argument_map.main_finding: Prepared-state directional depinning and protocol-specific vector winding arise in the reduced model; the sign survives tested compact/contact-compliance checks, boundary state selection can reverse it, and a weaker stationary mean current survives thermal mixing after exact winding identity becomes rare.
paper_argument_map.mechanism: Non-removable inversion-odd lateral registry content controls the directionality within the model, as shown by same-spectrum symmetrization and exact inversion.
paper_argument_map.implication: Registry symmetry, prepared state, boundary geometry and drive protocol jointly determine finite-contact directionality; compact similarity and boundary-state selection are distinct geometry regimes.
paper_argument_map.scope_boundary: No physical polarity law, universal friction constant, continuous global locking phase diagram, thermal critical point, full 3D atomistic validation or calibrated experimental unit conversion is established.
